questions.q: What did Sarah buy when the Doctor began to make money again?
choices: A new dress
A new hat for church
A piano for the parlor
New curtains for the house
questions.evidence: his sister, Sarah, bought a new dress

questions.q: Why did the Doctor keep getting more and more pets even after they got well?
choices: He paid them to stay and help him cure other animals
Many animals liked him so much they asked to stay, and he could not refuse
He wanted to start a circus of his own in the big garden
Their owners never came back to take them home again
questions.evidence: he never had the heart to refuse them

questions.q: Why did the Doctor take the monkey away from the organ-grinder?
choices: The monkey asked him in monkey-language to buy him
The organ-grinder wanted to sell the monkey for a shilling
The monkey's collar was too tight and he was dirty and unhappy
The monkey was sick and needed medicine for a cough
questions.evidence: the monkey's collar was too tight

questions.q: The animals named the monkey "Chee-Chee." What does that word mean in monkey-language?
choices: Little one
Friend
Ginger
Clever

questions.q: Why did the crocodile escape from the circus and come to the Doctor's garden?
choices: He wanted to eat the fish in the pond
He was looking for a way home to Africa
He had a bad tooth-ache
The circus-men had been cruel to him
questions.evidence: the crocodile who had a bad tooth-ache escaped at night

questions.q: What happened when the circus-men came to take the crocodile back?
choices: The Doctor paid them money so the crocodile could stay
The crocodile got so wild and savage that he frightened them away
The crocodile hid under Sarah's bed until they gave up and left
The crocodile went back with them but escaped again the next night
questions.evidence: he got so wild and savage that he frightened them away

questions.q: What did Sarah say she would do if the Doctor did not send the crocodile away?
choices: Go back to live with her family in Oxenthorpe
Go and get married
Call the circus-men to come and take it
Sell the house and garden

questions.q: How did the Doctor feel about having very little money after Sarah left?
choices: He did not worry, saying money did not matter as long as they were happy
He was very worried and stayed awake every night counting his coins
He was angry and blamed the animals for driving his sister away
He was ashamed and stopped walking through the town in his high hat
questions.evidence: What does money matter, so long as we are happy?

questions.q: Which animal was chosen to keep the accounts because it was good at arithmetic?
choices: Dab-Dab the duck
Polynesia the parrot
Too-Too the owl
Gub-Gub the pig
questions.evidence: the owl, Too-Too, was to keep the accounts

questions.q: Why did Chee-Chee find his new housework easier than the other animals did?
choices: He had worked in the circus and was used to hard work
He was the oldest and knew how to keep a house
He had hands and could do things like a man
He only had to do the gardening, which was easy
questions.evidence: who had hands, and could do things like a man

questions.q: How did Jip sweep the floors?
choices: He pushed a small broom along with his nose
He brushed the dust out of the door with his paws
He swept with his tail, with a rag tied onto it
He carried a feather duster in his mouth
questions.evidence: sweeping his tail over the floor with a rag tied onto it for a broom

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: How the crocodile learned to live happily in the fish-pond
How the Doctor lost his money again, and the animals worked to help him
How the Doctor rescued the monkey from a cruel organ-grinder
How the animals sold radishes and roses at a stall by the gate
questions.evidence: it is for our sakes that the old man finds himself so lonely and so poor
